sections.title: Right now
lines: Pre-race growth. Green flag Fri 10/16 6:30 PM CT (in 1d 19h).
Sold 4,443 contracts so far; 30,008 more resting on the book. Premium collected $519.
Worst line is -$945. The glide target right now is -$400, so it is $545 short; the final target is -$100 by T-60.
Backstop is ON for Chandler Smith: their lines are under -$400, so they stop adding until the others catch up.
Prices follow Bovada, refreshed every 5m (last 3m ago). Covers 35 of 36 drivers.
The bot is running slow: it is set to check every 30s but its heartbeat only moves about every 53s. Slow reads and rate limits do this; timed steps can land a little late.

sections.title: Lagging sides
lines: Christian Eckes: sold 0, 1,464 behind the leader. Cheapest row 10c; the crowd has been buying at 10c; fair 9.8c. Already at its floor (about 10c); it will not go lower unless the crowd price or fair drops.
Ty Majeski: sold 0, 1,464 behind the leader. Cheapest row 8c; the crowd has been buying at 8c; fair 7.9c. Already at its floor (about 8c); it will not go lower unless the crowd price or fair drops.

Kaden Honeycutt: sold 281, 1,183 behind the leader. Cheapest row 14c; the crowd has been buying at 16c; fair 11.5c. Already at its floor (about 16c); it will not go lower unless the crowd price or fair drops.

Layne Riggs: sold 678, 786 behind the leader. Cheapest row 29c; the crowd has been buying at 25.4c; fair 28.1c. It can step down 1c at a time, to no lower than about 26.1c, after 20 min with no fill, at most one step per 15 min. Last step: none seen.

Brent Crews: sold 706, 758 behind the leader. Cheapest row 7c; the crowd has been buying at n/a; fair 5.2c. It can step down 1c at a time, to no lower than about 3.2c, after 20 min with no fill, at most one step per 15 min. Last step: none seen.

The bot checks every 53s; it logs a market snapshot every 10 min. Rows already resting are not repriced when the sportsbook moves; only new rows use the fresh price. A step is skipped if filling the new row in full would push a line under the backstop or the glide target.
From T-360 (glide start) the price-step rule is on for lagging drivers so they can sell into the late rush of crowd orders.

sections.title: Next wave of contracts
lines: Trigger: when a driver's current wave is 90% filled and a full fill would keep his line above the gate, the bot posts the next wave (sizes 1,000/750/750 for contenders/midfield/long shots per wave), priced one cent above the last fill. The book's worst line must also be above the backstop, and free cash above the $400 floor.
Right now it is the growth phase (before T-360): the gate is loose (-$1,000) and the number of contracts is limited by what the crowd is likely to buy and by free cash.
Tristan McKee: 2 waves so far, 1,240 contracts offered in all; the latest (490 at 3c) is 0% filled.
Latest wave note (1h 31m ago): Tristan McKee: wave 1 100% filled; 510 @ 0.03 fits the growth gate but the free cash $87.23 over the $400 floor funds only 0
Waves stop at T-60.

sections.title: Tightening
lines: The risk glide starts at T-360 (Fri 10/16 12:30 PM CT, in 1d 13h). Until then the limit on the worst line is the backstop (-$400). From then the limit slides in a straight line to -$100 at T-60 (Fri 10/16 5:30 PM CT).

When the worst line is under the target the bot: blocks any post whose full fill would break the target, shrinks resting size over the room in place, buys back the worst line cheaply (only when each dollar spent lifts the line 2.0x or more, up to 3 per loop, budget 50% of banked premium), and starts selling to close gaps from T-90.
Preview: if the worst line is still -$945 at T-360, the glide would have to bring it up by about $545 to reach the first target.
Even-up (lagging drivers re-priced to fair) from T-60; the take window (sell to close gaps) from T-20 to the green flag.
Checkpoints: T-2880, T-1440, T-360, T-180, T-120, T-60, T-20 before the green flag.
At the green flag the bot keeps the resting orders and hands over to the in-race engine.

sections.title: Will it adapt on its own?
lines: Yes, on its own: new waves for popular drivers, price steps on lagging contenders, the backstop that stops a heavy driver, and the glide that tightens the worst line toward -$100.

No, it will not: reprice a resting row when Bovada moves, or buy back a driver for any reason except the glide's cheap-lift rule. If Bovada's field drops below 80% coverage the bot just holds what it has.

The one thing that depends on the market: the worst line is -$945 against a -$100 final target. Premium from the rest of the field and fills on lagging drivers lift it; the glide's buybacks cover what is left, within their budget. It might not fully close.
I only read the bot's settings, state and log. I cannot see its next decision, only the rules it follows.
